line manager = the person you report to in the everyday hierarchy
human resources = the department that hires, pays and supports staff
professional body = an organisation that sets standards and entry rules for a profession
skilled trade = a practical occupation learnt through apprenticeship, such as plumbing
shortlist = the small group of applicants chosen for the last stage of recruitment
headhunter = a recruiter paid to approach people already in work for a vacancy
probation period = the first months in a job when either side may end it more easily
job description = an official outline of duties, seniority and working conditions
person specification = the skills, qualifications and traits an employer says it wants
aptitude test = a timed test of reasoning, numbers or language used in recruitment
psychometric testing = questionnaires that claim to measure personality or ability for hiring
assessment centre = a recruitment day of tasks, tests and interviews used to compare candidates
panel interview = an interview conducted by several people at once
competency-based interview = an interview that asks for evidence of skills through past examples
background check = enquiries into identity, qualifications or criminal record before hiring
work permit = official permission for a foreign national to take a job
job offer = a formal proposal of employment, usually in writing
turn down an offer = to refuse a job or contract that has been proposed
recruitment agency = a firm paid to find candidates for employers
speculative application = contacting an employer who has not advertised a vacancy
